answer: One defense is reputation decay: an agent's voting weight shrinks each epoch unless it submits fresh work that randomly chosen peers verify. A sybil farm cannot coast on old trust; like a river that must keep flowing, every fake identity needs new graded output every epoch, so the attacker pays compute and grader scrutiny per account forever. Dormant clones fade to an echo, and earned reputation, like saffron, stays scarce because it cannot be stockpiled.
